hard_problems.name: Integer Factorization
hard_problems.description: Recover factors of a composite integer.
hard_problems.statement: Given a composite integer $N$, find a divisor $d$ with $1<d<N$. Repeated splitting yields the prime factorization.

parameters.modulus: Composite $N$; the RSA setting uses $N=pq$ for distinct primes.
parameters.input_distribution: Specify how the prime factors and their sizes are sampled.

formulations.description: Find a nontrivial factor of the supplied composite integer.

qualifications: RSA moduli are one input family, not all composite integers. Factoring enables RSA inversion; the converse is not assumed.

references.locator: Sections VI and IX.A–D: modulus construction, factoring and alternative approaches.

hard_problems.name: RSA Problem
hard_problems.statement: Given $N=pq$, an exponent $e$ coprime to $\varphi(N)$, and $y\in\mathbb{Z}_N^*$, recover $x\in\mathbb{Z}_N^*$ such that $x^e\equiv y\pmod N$.

parameters.modulus: RSA modulus $N=pq$ with hidden distinct prime factors.
parameters.input_distribution: Specify modulus generation and the distribution of $y$ (usually uniform in $\mathbb{Z}_N^*$).

formulations.description: Recover an e-th root modulo the public RSA modulus.

qualifications: This is the RSA inversion problem, not OAEP decryption or PSS forgery. Factoring is sufficient to solve it, but general equivalence is not claimed.

references.locator: Sections VI and IX.D: exponentiation, decryption and direct recovery without factoring.

hard_problems.name: Discrete Logarithm
hard_problems.description: Recover an exponent in a specified cyclic group.
hard_problems.statement: Given a cyclic group $G=\langle g\rangle$ of order $r$ and $h\in G$, find $x\in\mathbb{Z}_r$ such that $g^x=h$.

parameters.group: Specify $G$, its encoding and generator $g$; finite-field subgroups are one family.
parameters.input_distribution: Specify the distribution of $x$ (commonly uniform in $\mathbb{Z}_r$).

formulations.description: Recover the exponent modulo the order of the generator.

qualifications: Group structure and representation affect algorithms. DLP, computational Diffie–Hellman and decisional Diffie–Hellman are distinct tasks.

references.locator: Section III, equations (4)–(8), p. 649: finite-field logarithms and key exchange.

hard_problems.name: Elliptic-Curve Discrete Logarithm
hard_problems.description: Recover a scalar in an elliptic-curve subgroup.
hard_problems.statement: Given an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{F}_q$, a point $P$ of order $r$, and $Q\in\langle P\rangle$, find $x\in\mathbb{Z}_r$ such that $[x]P=Q$.

parameters.curve: Field $\mathbb{F}_q$, curve equation and point encoding.
parameters.input_distribution: Specify how $x$ and hence $Q$ are sampled.

formulations.description: Recover the scalar modulo the subgroup order.

qualifications: This is a DLP family, not a complete security model for ECDH or signatures. Curve choice, subgroup membership and protocol assumptions remain explicit.

references.locator: Sections 5.5.1.2 and 5.6.1.2: elliptic-curve domain parameters and the relation Q = dG.

hard_problems.name: LWE
hard_problems.description: Noisy linear equations over modular vector spaces.
hard_problems.statement: In the discrete formulation, sample $A\leftarrow\mathbb{Z}_q^{m\times n}$ uniformly, a secret $s\in\mathbb{Z}_q^n$ and an error vector $e$. The observations are $(A,b)$ with $b=As+e\bmod q$.

parameters.sample_count: Number of equations $m$, or a stated sample-oracle budget.
parameters.secret_distribution: Distribution of $s$, e.g. uniform or an explicitly specified small-secret distribution.
parameters.error_distribution: Distribution and scale of $e$, including independence between samples.

formulations.description: Distinguish $(A,As+e)$ from uniformly sampled $(A,u)$ with the same dimensions.

qualifications: Hardness and search-to-decision reductions require parameter and distribution conditions; small-secret, binary-secret and noise-free cases are not interchangeable.

references.locator: Section 2: LWE distributions and search task; Section 4: decision variants.

hard_problems.name: Ring-LWE
hard_problems.description: Noisy ring products with an explicit embedding and error distribution.
hard_problems.statement: In the dual formulation, let $R=\mathcal{O}_K$, let $R^\vee$ be its codifferent, and set $T=K_{\mathbb{R}}/R^\vee$. For fixed $s\in R^\vee/qR^\vee$, samples have uniform $a\in R/qR$ and $b=as/q+e\bmod R^\vee$.

parameters.ring: Number field $K$ and ring of integers $R$.
parameters.sample_count: Number of independent ring samples or oracle budget.
parameters.secret_distribution: Distribution on $R^\vee/qR^\vee$; state the search or average-case convention.
parameters.error_distribution: Distribution on $K_{\mathbb{R}}$, including scale and embedding.
parameters.representation: Dual/codifferent formulation above; a polynomial or discrete encoding requires an explicit conversion and error distribution.

formulations.description: Recover $s$ from samples sharing that secret.
Distinguish secret-and-error samples from uniform samples over $(R/qR)\times T$.

qualifications: The cited decision problem samples both the secret and an error distribution. Search/decision equivalence and hardness guarantees depend on the field, error family and parameters.

references.locator: Section 3, Definitions 3.1–3.5; discussion following Definition 3.3 on dual and non-dual representations.

hard_problems.name: Module-LWE
hard_problems.description: Noisy linear equations over a module of a number ring.
hard_problems.statement: Let $R=\mathcal{O}_K$, $T=K_{\mathbb{R}}/R^\vee$ and $s\in(R^\vee/qR^\vee)^k$. Samples consist of uniform $a\in(R/qR)^k$ and $b=\langle a,s\rangle/q+e\bmod R^\vee$.

parameters.ring: Number field $K$ and its ring of integers $R$.
parameters.module_rank: Module rank $k$ over $R$, separate from the degree of $K$.
parameters.sample_count: Number of independent samples or oracle budget.
parameters.secret_distribution: Distribution of the shared module secret $s$.
parameters.representation: Dual formulation above; scheme-specific discrete module equations must state their ring, basis and distributions.

formulations.description: Distinguish the noisy samples from uniform samples over $(R/qR)^k\times T$.

qualifications: ML-KEM uses a particular discrete Module-LWE setting, not every parameter choice in this problem family. Ring degree and module rank are different parameters.

references.locator: Section 4.1, Definition 4.6: search and decision M-LWE; Theorem 4.7: parameter conditions.

hard_problems.name: SIS
hard_problems.description: Find a short nonzero vector in a random modular kernel.
hard_problems.statement: Given uniform $A\in\mathbb{Z}_q^{n\times m}$, find $z\in\mathbb{Z}^m$ with $Az\equiv0\pmod q$ and $0<\lVert z\rVert\le\beta$.

parameters.bound: Upper bound $\beta$ on the integer-vector norm.

formulations.description: Produce a nonzero integer solution satisfying both the modular equation and the norm bound.

qualifications: Parameters must allow a solution without making the task trivial; changing the norm or bound changes the problem. This is not inhomogeneous SIS.

references.locator: Section 3.1, Definition 3.1: SIS; Theorem 3.2: a parameter-dependent hardness reduction.

hard_problems.name: Module-SIS
hard_problems.description: Find a short nonzero module vector in a modular kernel.
hard_problems.statement: For $R=\mathcal{O}_K$ and uniform $A\in(R/qR)^{k\times m}$, find $z\in R^m$ with $Az=0\bmod qR$ and $0<\lVert z\rVert\le\beta$.

parameters.ring: Number field $K$ and ring of integers $R$.
parameters.norm: Specify the norm and its embedding or coefficient basis.
parameters.representation: The cited reduction uses the canonical embedding; coefficient norms require a stated basis and conversion.

formulations.description: Produce a nonzero short module vector satisfying the homogeneous modular equation.

qualifications: The ML-DSA association does not identify generic Module-SIS with all of its security assumptions, including self-target variants.

references.locator: Section 3.1, Definition 3.5: M-SIS; Section 2.1: canonical embedding and norms.

primitives.name: ChaCha20-Poly1305
primitives.description: Authenticated encryption combining the IETF ChaCha20 instance with Poly1305.

primitives.name: CMAC
primitives.description: Block-cipher-based message authentication; registered instances use AES with full tags.

primitives.name: RSAES-OAEP
primitives.description: RSA encryption with OAEP encoding. Profiles fix the modulus length, message hash, MGF1 hash and label.

primitives.name: SM2 Encryption
primitives.description: SM2 public-key encryption on the recommended prime-field curve, using SM3 for the KDF and integrity digest.

primitives.name: Finite-Field DH
primitives.description: Finite-field Diffie–Hellman over the RFC 7919 named safe-prime groups. Group registration does not specify authentication or a key-derivation protocol.

primitives.name: ECDH
primitives.description: Elliptic-curve shared-secret computation over the NIST prime-field curves; authentication and key derivation belong to the enclosing protocol.

primitives.name: X25519 / X448
primitives.description: RFC 7748 Montgomery-coordinate Diffie–Hellman functions with fixed scalar and coordinate encodings.

primitives.name: SM2 Key Exchange
primitives.description: SM2 key exchange combines static and ephemeral key pairs, identity digests and a KDF. It is not plain ECDH.

primitives.name: RSASSA-PSS
primitives.description: RSA signatures with PSS encoding. Profiles fix the message hash, MGF1 hash and salt length independently of OAEP.

primitives.name: ECDSA
primitives.description: Elliptic-curve digital signatures with a specified prime-field curve and message hash.

primitives.name: EdDSA
primitives.description: Pure EdDSA instances from RFC 8032. Ed25519/Ed448 signature encodings are distinct from X25519/X448 key-agreement encodings.

primitives.name: SM2 Signatures
primitives.description: SM2 digital signatures bind an identity digest and the message with SM3; the signing equation is distinct from ECDSA.

primitives.name: ML-DSA
primitives.description: Standardized module-lattice signatures. Directory instances identify FIPS 204 parameter sets, not pre-standard Dilithium variants.

primitives.name: SLH-DSA
primitives.description: Stateless hash-based signatures combining FORS and an XMSS hypertree. All twelve FIPS 205 SHA2/SHAKE parameter sets are registered.

primitives.name: ML-KEM
primitives.description: Standardized module-lattice key encapsulation with re-encryption checks and implicit rejection, distinct from its internal public-key encryption component.

primitives.name: uBlock
primitives.description: A PX-network block cipher designed for high-throughput software using nibble substitution, permutation and XOR operations.
primitives.parameter_scope: The three original profiles fix block/key widths and full-round counts; block width is written before key width.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: LOL2.0
primitives.description: Blockwise stream ciphers coupling an LFSR, nonlinear driving registers and an AES-round-based FSM. Mini uses the single configuration and Double the parallel-dual configuration.
primitives.parameter_scope: Default LFSR2 profiles only: Mini has a 128-bit IV and Double a 256-bit IV. The AES round operation is not a complete AES encryption instance.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: LOL2.0-SCMAC
primitives.description: Authenticated-encryption constructions applying SCMAC to LOL2.0-Mini and LOL2.0-Double, with separate authentication registers and final feedback.
primitives.parameter_scope: The concrete profiles select 128-bit tags and the default LFSR2 stream cores. Stream and authentication states are recorded separately.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: ElGamal Encryption
primitives.description: Randomized encryption in a cyclic group, with ciphertext components formed from an ephemeral exponent and a Diffie–Hellman mask.
primitives.parameter_scope: Section II. A concrete profile must select the group, encoding and message space. Textbook ElGamal is malleable and is not claimed to provide chosen-ciphertext security.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: Rabin Encryption
primitives.description: A public-key squaring function modulo a composite integer whose inversion is related to factorization.
primitives.parameter_scope: Public-key-function construction. Fix the modulus distribution, message encoding, padding and root-selection rule before registering an encryption instance. Raw squaring is not a complete secure encryption profile.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: Paillier
primitives.description: Probabilistic encryption modulo n squared with an additive homomorphic operation on plaintexts.
primitives.parameter_scope: Scheme 1 and its parameter conditions. Fix the modulus size, generator, randomness domain and message encoding; do not assume g = n + 1 or an arbitrary modulus length.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: Cramer–Shoup
primitives.description: Public-key encryption combining two group generators, a universal one-way hash family and a consistency check for chosen-ciphertext resistance under the specified assumptions.
primitives.parameter_scope: Basic scheme and security theorem. A profile must bind the prime-order group, two generators, hash-family selection, encodings and validation rules.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: ECIES
primitives.description: An elliptic-curve integrated encryption scheme deriving encryption and authentication keys from ephemeral–static key agreement.
primitives.parameter_scope: SEC 1 v2, Section 5.1. Curve, point validation, cofactor option, KDF, symmetric cipher, MAC and shared-information encodings must be chosen together.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: MQV / ECMQV
primitives.description: Authenticated key agreement combining static and ephemeral public keys; the cited SEC 1 definition is its elliptic-curve form ECMQV.
primitives.parameter_scope: SEC 1 v2, Sections 3.4 and 6.2. Fix a domain-parameter set, validation and cofactor rules, key derivation and identity-binding protocol before registering an instance.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: HMQV
primitives.description: Hashed MQV-style authenticated Diffie–Hellman with identity-dependent hash challenges.
primitives.parameter_scope: Protocol definition and security model in the original paper. Group, hash outputs, identity encodings, public-key validation and protocol variant are profile choices, not implicit ECDH parameters.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: Schnorr Signatures
primitives.description: Signatures obtained from a discrete-logarithm identification protocol by hashing the commitment and message into a challenge.
primitives.parameter_scope: Identification and signature algorithms in the original paper. Group, challenge hash, encoding and nonce-generation policy are not fixed by the family name. BIP340 has a separate concrete family.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: BLS Signatures
primitives.description: Short pairing-based signatures that map a message into a group and exponentiate it by a signing secret.
primitives.parameter_scope: Original signature construction. Fix the pairing curve, source-group orientation, hash-to-curve ciphersuite, subgroup checks and basic/augmentation/proof-of-possession mode. Aggregation policies are not interchangeable.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: GOST R 34.10-2012
primitives.description: Elliptic-curve signatures defined by the GOST R 34.10-2012 signing and verification equations.
primitives.parameter_scope: RFC 7091, Sections 5–6. The 256-bit and 512-bit families need exact named domain parameters, GOST hash selection and public-key/signature serialization before a concrete profile is registered.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: SM9 Encryption
primitives.description: Identity-based encryption using a trusted key-generation center and bilinear pairings.
primitives.parameter_scope: GB/T 38635.2-2020, encryption and decryption algorithms. Fix master parameters, identity encoding, encryption mode, KDF and ciphertext format; XOR and block-cipher modes are distinct profiles.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: SM9 Signatures
primitives.description: Identity-based signatures using pairing groups and signing keys derived by a trusted key-generation center.
primitives.parameter_scope: GB/T 38635.2-2020, signature and verification algorithms. Fix system parameters, identity and purpose identifiers, hash functions and point encodings; do not merge this identity with SM9 encryption.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: SM9 Key Exchange
primitives.description: Identity-based authenticated key exchange using pairings, identity-derived private keys and ephemeral contributions.
primitives.parameter_scope: GB/T 38635.2-2020, key-exchange protocol. Bind master parameters, participant identities, KDF output length, confirmation mode and point validation before adding a concrete session profile.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: DSA
primitives.description: Finite-field digital signatures with a prime-order subgroup and per-message secret nonce.
primitives.parameter_scope: Historical FIPS 186-4 L/N pairs with SHA-256. Group generation and signature serialization are not fixed by these size profiles.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: BIP340 Schnorr
primitives.description: A byte-level Schnorr signature scheme over secp256k1 using x-only public keys, tagged SHA-256 and fixed 64-byte signatures.
primitives.parameter_scope: BIP340 only; distinct from generic Schnorr, ECDSA, multisignature protocols and transaction policy.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5
primitives.description: RSA signatures with deterministic EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 encoding. This is a signature scheme, not RSAES-PKCS1-v1_5 encryption.
primitives.parameter_scope: Profiles select a modulus length and SHA-256; the public exponent and key-generation method remain explicit analysis assumptions.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: Falcon
primitives.description: NTRU-lattice signatures with fast Fourier sampling and compressed short-vector signatures.
primitives.parameter_scope: Falcon v1.2, padded signature encoding. These submission identities are not aliases for a future final FN-DSA profile.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: XMSS
primitives.description: Stateful Merkle-tree signatures using WOTS+ one-time signatures.
primitives.parameter_scope: RFC 8391 SHA2/256 sets with heights 10, 16 and 20, approved by SP 800-208. Signing state must be persisted; reusing a one-time key invalidates the security conditions.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: XMSSMT
primitives.description: A multi-tree extension of XMSS that authenticates lower-tree roots with upper-tree WOTS+ keys.
primitives.parameter_scope: Selected SHA2/256 total-height/layer pairs 20/2, 40/4 and 60/6; each layer has equal height. Signing state must be persisted; reusing a one-time key invalidates the security conditions.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: LMS
primitives.description: Stateful Merkle-tree signatures using LM-OTS one-time signatures.
primitives.parameter_scope: SHA256/M32 tree heights 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 with LMOTS SHA256/N32/W8. LMOTS w is a digit width in bits, not the WOTS+ base. Signing state must be persisted; reusing a one-time key invalidates the security conditions.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: HSS
primitives.description: Hierarchical signatures that authenticate lower-level LMS public keys with higher-level LMS signatures.
primitives.parameter_scope: Two identical LMS layers, height 10 or 15 per layer, with SHA256/M32 and LMOTS SHA256/N32/W8. Other heterogeneous hierarchies are not implied. Signing state must be persisted; reusing a one-time key invalidates the security conditions.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: HQC
primitives.description: Code-based KEM combining a quasi-cyclic encryption structure with concatenated error-correcting codes.
primitives.parameter_scope: HQC-1/3/5 are version-5.1 profiles with 32-byte seeded decapsulation keys; not the earlier NIST-round parameter identities.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: FrodoKEM
primitives.description: A KEM based on unstructured Learning with Errors and dense matrices.
primitives.parameter_scope: Salted FrodoKEM, not eFrodoKEM; matrix generation uses AES-128 or SHAKE128. Exact mapping to final ISO parameter profiles remains pending.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: Classic McEliece
primitives.description: A Niederreiter-form KEM based on binary Goppa codes, with large systematic public keys and compact syndrome ciphertexts.
primitives.parameter_scope: The f suffix changes key generation, not public-key/ciphertext sizes. Exact mapping to final ISO parameter profiles remains pending.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: NTRU
primitives.description: NTRU-HPS and NTRU-HRSS key encapsulation over polynomial quotient rings.
primitives.parameter_scope: Four pinned 2019 KEM profiles. Original NTRUEncrypt and NTRU Prime are separate constructions; this is not a claim to catalogue every later NTRU revision.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: NTRU Prime
primitives.description: Streamlined NTRU Prime KEMs using quotient rings defined by x^p − x − 1.
primitives.parameter_scope: Six sntrup sets only; NTRU LPRime and earlier encodings are not conflated. Categories reproduce Section 8 strategy #1, including its model-dependent qualifications.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: SABER
primitives.description: Module-LWR key encapsulation with power-of-two moduli and rounding-based compression.
primitives.parameter_scope: LightSaber, Saber and FireSaber use the full secret-key encoding, not the optional compressed lengths in parentheses. Target categories are the submission claims, not an independent security assessment.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.

primitives.name: BIKE
primitives.description: Quasi-cyclic MDPC code-based KEM using iterative bit-flipping decoding.
primitives.parameter_scope: Pinned round-four profiles. The source permits several secret-key representations; no single secret-key byte length is fabricated. Non-selection is not withdrawal.

inclusion.note: Added in the November 2026 coverage expansion; no citation-count threshold or security endorsement is asserted.
